exports: pub fn lex_number<'a>(input: &'a [u8], offset: u32, policy: &NumericPolicy) -> Result<NumberToken<'a>>

test_vectors.coverage: Accepted integer, fraction, exponent, and quoted-integer spellings
test_vectors.assertions: Exact raw bytes and borrowing pointer, full source span, kind, sign, integer and fraction digit counts, explicit exponent, and quoted status

test_vectors.coverage: Integer magnitudes at and beyond u64 and i64 limits
test_vectors.assertions: Lexical acceptance without imposing converter magnitude limits

test_vectors.coverage: Malformed grammar and incomplete required components
test_vectors.assertions: Leading plus and zeros, absent digits, hexadecimal and binary forms, underscores, whitespace inside required components, NaN, Infinity, invalid suffixes, controls, and non-ASCII bytes produce InvalidNumber at the first offending byte or EOF

test_vectors.coverage: All 256 byte values after a complete exponent and a quoted integer
test_vectors.assertions: Only space, tab, CR, LF, comma, right bracket, and right brace delimit tokens; appended exponent digits extend the unquoted spelling
Reject disabled quotes, fractions, exponents, escapes, internal whitespace, malformed digits, and invalid post-quote boundaries; distinguish missing digits from a missing closing quote

test_vectors.coverage: Nonzero start offsets and source provenance
test_vectors.assertions: Absolute spans and error offsets, quoted wrappers included in spans but excluded from raw bytes, exact-offset scanning, no inspection after a valid delimiter, and unchanged input and caller policy
Empty input and offsets at EOF, beyond EOF, and u32::MAX; negative exponent limits including i16::MIN reject at the requested token start before EOF or grammar validation

test_vectors.coverage: Exponent policy limits and overflow resistance
test_vectors.assertions: Inclusive positive and negative bounds at 308 and 32767, rejection immediately beyond bounds, leading zeros, exponent magnitudes beyond i32 and u32, and errors at the first exponent digit

test_vectors.coverage: Zero exponent limit and long inputs
test_vectors.assertions: 8192-byte exponent spellings preserve arbitrarily many leading zeros; 8192-digit integers and 8189-digit fractions have exact counts without a fixed digit cap
Integer and fraction digits determine zero independently of the explicit exponent; errors point to the minus sign including inside quotes; grammar and boundary errors precede value constraints
The non-finite conversion flag does not change lexical acceptance of valid large decimal spellings
